Rashi on Bava Kamma 45a:10:1.english: If he safeguarded it - [With] superior safeguarding.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 45a:10:2.hebrew: כולהו נמי ניפטרו - מדמי שור, בר משואל, דהא אנוסין הם:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 45a:10:2.english: All of them should also be exempt - from [paying] the value of the ox, except for a borrower, for they are [in a situation of] unavoidable accident.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 45a:11:1.english: Reduced safeguarding - A door that can withstand an ordinary wind.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 45a:11:2.hebrew: כלתה ליה שמירתו - דאין עליו להתחזק בשמירתו, ודי בכך, ולאו פשיעה היא. הלכך, לגבי בעלים פטור מדמי שור, דהא סגי ליה בשמירה פחותה, ובעי כפרה:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 45a:11:2.english: His safeguarding is fulfilled - For he is not obligated to strengthen his safeguarding, and this is sufficient, and it is not [considered] negligence. Therefore, with respect to the owner, he is exempt from [paying] the value of the ox, for reduced safeguarding suffices for him, and he requires atonement.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 45a:11:3.hebrew: והני לא כלתה שמירתן - שחייבין היו להתחזק בשמירתו שיהא שמור לבעליו, ופשיעה היא, מידי דהוה אגניבה ואבידה:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 45a:11:3.english: And these have not fulfilled their safeguarding - For they were obligated to strengthen [their] safeguarding of it so that it would be guarded for its owner, and it is [considered] negligence, just like [in the case of] theft and loss.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 45a:12:1.hebrew: כמאן אי כר"מ - דאמר במתניתין מועד לא סגי ליה בשמירה פחותה, ומשום הכי נמי קתני משלמין כופר:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 45a:12:1.english: In accordance with whom? If in accordance with Rabbi Meir - Who said in our Mishnah [that for] a mu'ad [ox], inferior guarding does not suffice, and for that reason [the baraita] also teaches [that they] pay kofer [ransom].

Rashi on Bava Kamma 45a:1:1.english: [It is] sold - It is [sold] for plowing.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 45a:1:2.english: [If] he consecrated it, it is consecrated - And the practical difference [is] that if one derives benefit from it, he has committed misuse [of consecrated property].

Rashi on Bava Kamma 45a:1:3.hebrew: מוחזר - ואע"ג דשקלי ליה בי דינא, הוי שומר פטור, דהא כשהחזירו שור מעליא הוא:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 45a:1:3.english: Returned - And even though the court takes it, the bailee is exempt, for when he returned it, it was a proper ox.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 45a:2:1.english: It is not consecrated - For it does not stand in its owner's domain to consecrate it.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 45a:3:1.hebrew: אין אומרין באיסורי הנאה הרי שלך לפניך - ונפקא מיניה לגזל חמץ ועבר עליו הפסח, והחזירו — אינו מוחזר:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 45a:3:1.english: One does not say with regard to items prohibited from benefit, "That which is yours is before you" - And the practical difference is regarding [one who] stole leavened bread [chametz] and Passover passed over it, and he returned it — it is not [considered] returned.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 45a:4:1.hebrew: דא"כ - דלרבנן אין אומרין:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 45a:4:1.english: For if [it were] so - That according to the Rabbis, one does not say [so].

Rashi on Bava Kamma 45a:4:2.hebrew: ליפלגו - רבנן בחמץ בפסח ולימרו דחייב, ואנן קיימא לן בהגוזל עצים (לקמן בבא קמא ד' צח:) דלרבנן אומר לו "הרי שלך לפניך", דקתני: גזל חמץ ועבר עליו הפסח והחזירו, וכן שור עד שלא נגמר דינו - אומרין לו "הרי שלך לפניך", אבל משנגמר - לא. והא סברא לרבנן הוא דשמיעא להו, וקתני דבחמץ בפסח מודו דאמרינן באיסורי הנאה "הרי שלך לפניך". אלא דכולי עלמא אמרינן באיסורי הנאה "הרי שלך לפניך" היכא דאיסורא ממילא אתא ליה, כגון חמץ בפסח, ולא מצי א"ל "האי לאו מידי הוא". אבל הכא, משום הכי אמרי רבנן אינו מוחזר, דאמר ליה "אתפסתיה לתוראי כו'", והזיקא דבידים הוא שהביאו לבי דינא. והאי דנקט "אי אהדרתיה ניהליה", לאו משום דחיובא דלא אהדריה הוא, דא"כ, בחמץ בפסח נמי לימא ליה "אי אהדרתיה ניהלי הוה אכילנא ליה"; ועוד, לר' יעקב נמי, נהי דגומרים דינו של שור שלא בפניו, נימא ליה "אי אהדרתיה ניהלי הוה שחיטנא ליה"! אלא אדלא אהדריה לא מחייבי ליה רבנן, דהא קמהדר ליה השתא, ואמרינן באיסורי הנאה "הרי שלך לפניך". אלא חיוביה משום דהוליכו לב"ד בידים, והכי קאמר ליה: לא היה לך להוליכו לב"ד, דאי הוה בידי הוה מערקנא ליה מינייהו:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 45a:4:2.english: Let them dispute - [i.e.,] the Rabbis, regarding leavened bread on Passover, and say that he is liable! Yet we hold as an established law in [the chapter] HaGozel Eitzim (later, Bava Kamma 98b) that according to the Rabbis he says to him, "That which is yours is before you," as it is taught [in a Baraita]: If one stole leavened bread and Passover passed over it and he returned it, and similarly [if one stole] an ox before its verdict was finalized, they say to him, "That which is yours is before you"; but once [its verdict] was finalized, no. And this reasoning was heard [as the view of] the Rabbis, and [yet] it teaches that regarding leavened bread on Passover they concede that we say with regard to items from which it is prohibited to derive benefit, "That which is yours is before you." Rather, according to everyone we say with regard to items from which it is prohibited to derive benefit, "That which is yours is before you," where the prohibition came upon it on its own, such as leavened bread on Passover, and [the owner] cannot say to him, "This is worth nothing." Here, however, this is the reason the Rabbis say it is not [considered] returned: because [the owner] says to him, "You have handed my ox over, etc.," and it is direct damage with his own hands that he brought it to court. And that which he mentioned, "If you had returned it to me," is not because the liability is for not having returned it; for if so, regarding leavened bread on Passover as well, let him say to him, "If you had returned it to me, I would have eaten it"! And furthermore, according to Rabbi Yaakov too, granted that they finalize the verdict of an ox in its absence, let [the owner] say to him, "If you had returned it to me, I would have slaughtered it"! Rather, for not having returned it the Rabbis do not hold him liable, since he is returning it to him now, and we say with regard to items from which it is prohibited to derive benefit, "That which is yours is before you." Rather, his liability is because he brought it to court with his own hands, and this is what he says to him: "You should not have brought it to court, for had it been in my possession, I would have made it flee from them."

Rashi on Bava Kamma 45a:6:1.english: Ultimately, they would have issued its verdict - Therefore, it is damage [that came about] on its own, and not [done] with [his own] hands.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 45a:7:1.english: Just as the owners [are judged] in their presence - As it is written: “Until he stands before the congregation for judgment” (Numbers 35:12).

Tosafot on Bava Kamma 45a:10:1.hebrew: אפילו כולהו נמי ליפטרו - ושואל גופיה, נהי דחייב לשלם דמי שור לבעלים, מ"מ כופר אין משלם:
Tosafot on Bava Kamma 45a:10:1.english: Even all of them should also be exempt - And [as for] the borrower himself, although he is obligated to pay the value of the ox to the owner, in any event he does not pay ransom [kofer].

Tosafot on Bava Kamma 45a:1:1.hebrew: מכור - פי' בקונטרס לרדיא, ומשנגמר דינו אינו מכור דאסור בהנאה. ואפילו ר"ת דמפרש דמחיים לא מיתסר, מ"מ הרי אסור להשהותו לענות דינו. ובמהדורא אחת פרש"י: מכרו מכור, דאמר ליה מוכר: "היה לך לשוחטו, כיון שידעת שהרג, ואת הוא דאפסדת אנפשך, ולא הוי מקח טעות". וא"ת: וסיפא, כשנגמר דינו, דקתני "אינו מכור" — מסתמא יודע שנגח ושנגמר דינו, דומיא דרישא שיודע שהרג; וא"כ ליהוי מעות מתנה, כמו במקדש אחותו? וי"ל: שאין הכל בקיאין בדין שור הנסקל, וסבור שיכול להשהותו לעשות בו מלאכתו, או אפילו לשחטו סבור דשרי:
Tosafot on Bava Kamma 45a:1:1.english: It is sold - The Kuntres [Rashi] explained [that it is sold] for plowing, whereas once its verdict has been finalized it is not sold, because it is forbidden for benefit. And even [according to] Rabbeinu Tam, who explains that while alive it is not forbidden [for benefit], nevertheless it is indeed forbidden to keep it alive [and] delay its execution. And in one edition [of his commentary], Rashi explained: His sale is valid [lit., sold], because the seller says to him: "You should have slaughtered it, since you knew that it had killed [a person], and it is you who caused the loss to yourself, and it is not a mistaken transaction." And if you will say: In the latter clause [of the Mishnah], when its verdict has been finalized, where it teaches "it is not sold," presumably [the buyer] knows that it gored and that its verdict was finalized, similar to the first clause where he knows that it killed; and if so, let the money be [considered] a gift, just as in the case of one who betroths his sister? One can say [in answer]: Not everyone is expert in the law of an ox that is to be stoned, and [the buyer] thinks that he can keep it to do his work with it, or even to slaughter it — he thinks that it is permitted.

Tosafot on Bava Kamma 45a:4:1.hebrew: דאם כן ליפלוג בחמץ בפסח - פ"ה: ואנן קי"ל בהגוזל [עצים] (לקמן בבא קמא דף צח:) דלרבנן אומר "הרי שלך לפניך", דקתני בברייתא: גזל חמץ ועבר עליו הפסח, שור והחזירו עד שלא נגמר דינו — אומר לו "הרי שלך לפניך", אבל משנגמר דינו — לא. והאי סברא לרבנן הוא דשמעינן להו, וקתני דבחמץ בפסח מודו. וקשה לפירושו, דסוגיא דהכא איתא נמי התם בהאי שמעתא, ומוכח התם דרבה — שדחה ואמר דכ"ע אומרים באיסורי הנאה "הרי שלך לפניך" מדלא פליגי בחמץ בפסח — לא היה יודע אותה ברייתא, אלא רבה בר שמואל הביאה, ואמר ליה רב חסדא: אי משכחת להו לא תימא להו. ואור"י דדייק מדלא פליגי בחמץ — שלא הייתי יכול לטעות ולהעמיד מחלוקתם במילתא אחריתי:
Tosafot on Bava Kamma 45a:4:1.english: For if so, let them dispute about leavened bread on Passover - Rashi explains: And we hold in [the chapter] HaGozel [Etzim] (below, Bava Kamma 98b) that according to the Rabbis one says "that which is yours is before you," as it is taught in a baraita: "If one stole leavened bread and Passover passed over it, [or] an ox and returned it before its verdict was finalized, he says to him: 'That which is yours is before you'; but after its verdict was finalized — no." And this reasoning is what we heard regarding the Rabbis, and [the baraita] teaches that regarding leavened bread on Passover they agree [that one says "that which is yours is before you"]. But [this] is difficult according to his explanation: for the sugya here is also [found] there in that discussion, and it is proven there that Rabbah — who pushed aside [the previous suggestion] and said that everyone says with regard to items from which it is prohibited to derive benefit "that which is yours is before you," [inferring this] from the fact that they do not dispute regarding leavened bread on Passover — did not know that baraita; rather, Rabbah bar Shmuel brought it, and Rav Chisda said to him: "If you find them, do not tell them [about this baraita]." And Rabbeinu Yitzchak explains that [Rabbah] infers [this] from the fact that they do not dispute regarding leavened bread [on Passover], [a case] where I would not have been able to err and establish their dispute in something else.

Tosafot on Bava Kamma 45a:5:1.hebrew: השתא אתפסתיה לתוראי - פי' הקונטרס: אתפסתיה בידים, שמסרו לב"ד לדונו בסקילה, ולכך אין יכול לומר לו "הרי שלך לפניך", לפי שהתפיסו בידים. והשתא לפי זה נוכל להעמיד כל הבבא דמתני' בהגוזל קמא (לקמן בבא קמא ד' צו:) כרבנן דרבי יעקב לפי דחוי דרבא, ושור היוצא ליסקל דקתני במתני' דהתם דא"ל "הרי שלך לפניך" — כגון שתפסוהו ב"ד מאליהן. ומיהו רש"י פי' שם שאין מעמיד כרבנן רק רישא, אבל הסיפא ד"שור היוצא ליסקל" דמתניתין לא אתיא כרבנן אלא כר' יעקב דוקא. וזה פי' משום שרוצה להעמיד "שור היוצא ליסקל" דמתניתין בתפיסה בידים ליד ב"ד, דומיא דברייתא, דהיינו בהתפיסו בידים. וקשה לפירושו: דאם זה ההיזק לא הוי היזק ניכר — אפילו אתפסיה בידים לא יתחייב; ואם הוא ניכר — אפילו תפסו ב"ד מאליהן למה יפטר? וכי לא היה לו לשומרו שלא יבא לידי כך? ועוד, דאם הוא פטור כשתופסים אותו מאליהן — כשתופסים אותו בידים נמי פטור, דסוף סוף אפילו לא היה מתפיסו בידים היו תופסים אותו מאליהן, ולא הפסידו בעלים בהתפסתו כלום. ונראה לר"י דבתפסוהו מאליהן נמי חייב, דמה שנופל ליד ב"ד חשוב היזק ניכר, וכיון דעל ידי פשיעה נפל ליד ב"ד — חייב ולא יכול לומר "הרי שלך לפניך", כמו בחמץ ועבר עליו הפסח שהוא היזק שאינו ניכר, הלכך יכול לומר שם "הרי שלך לפניך". ור' יעקב לא חשיב היזק ניכר מה שנופל ליד ב"ד וגמרו את דינו, כיון שאפילו לא בא לידם היו גומרין את דינו; ונמצא שאינו מפסיד ע"י שבא לידם, אלא כאילו גמרו דינו שלא בפניו חשיב, לפי שגם אז היה נאסר והוי היזק שאין ניכר, ולכך יכול לומר לו "הרי שלך לפניך" כמו בחמץ ועבר עליו הפסח. ו"אי אהדרתיה" לאו נתינת טעם הוא שהיה יכול להצילו ע"י כך, שאין תלוי בזה כמו שפ"ה, אלא כלומר: לא היו גומרין דינו שלא בפניו, ועכשיו גרמת שנתפס בידם וגומרין דינו ע"י מה שנפל בידם; וכיון שנפסד ע"י מה שנפל בידם, חשיב היזק ניכר ולא תוכל לומר "הרי שלך לפניך". וכן משמע בהניזקין (גיטין ד' נג:) דבהיזק ניכר אין יכול לומר "הרי שלך לפניך", דפריך ממתני' ד"גזל מטבע ונפסל כו'": "ואי אמרת היזק שאין ניכר שמיה היזק" — פי', משום דחשיב כאילו ניכר — "אמאי אומר ליה הרי שלך לפניך? גזל הוא וממונא מעליא בעי לשלומי", כי אין זה ממון שגזל, כיון שחשוב כאילו ההיזק ניכר בו, שאין לך שינוי גדול מזה אילו היה ניכר. ושור תם דמזיק ברשות שומר, אפילו קודם גמר דין אם יחזירנו שומר לבעלים — לא יפטר בכך, כיון דמזיק ע"י פשיעת שומר ונפל ברשות ניזק, להחליט לו מיד לר"ע להשתעבד בו ולרבי ישמעאל לגבות מגופו; והוה ליה היזק ניכר שהוא מופסד שנפל ברשות אחרים, ולא יכול לומר "הרי שלך לפניך", כמו שיכול לומר בשור שהרג אפילו לאחר גמר דין לר' יעקב, ולרבנן קודם גמר דין, ובחמץ לכ"ע:
Tosafot on Bava Kamma 45a:5:1.english: Now you have let my ox be seized - Rashi explained [that it means], "you handed it over with [your own] hands," [meaning] that he delivered it to the court to judge it for stoning, and therefore [the bailee] cannot say to him, "Here is yours before you," because he handed it over with [his own] hands. And now, according to this, we can establish the entire clause of the Mishnah in [the chapter] HaGozel Kamma (below, Bava Kamma 96b) in accordance with the Rabbis who disagree with Rabbi Yaakov, according to Rava's deflection; and [the case of] "an ox that is going out to be stoned," which is taught in the Mishnah there where [the robber] says to him, "Here is yours before you," [is] such as where the court seized it on their own. However, Rashi explained there that he establishes only the first clause in accordance with the Rabbis, whereas the latter clause of "an ox that is going out to be stoned" in our Mishnah does not accord with the Rabbis, but rather exclusively with Rabbi Yaakov. And he explained this because he wishes to establish "an ox that is going out to be stoned" of our Mishnah as [referring to] a seizure with [one's own] hands into the hand of the court, similar to the Baraita, which is [where] he handed it over with [his own] hands. And this explanation is difficult: for if this damage is not considered discernible damage (hezek nikkar), even if he handed it over with [his own] hands he should not be liable; and if it is discernible, even if the court seized it on their own, why should he be exempt — was it not his duty to guard it so that it would not come to this? And furthermore, if he is exempt when they seize it on their own, he should also be exempt when they seize it through his own hands, for after all, even if he had not handed it over with [his own] hands, they would have seized it on their own, and he did not cause the owners any loss by handing it over. And it appears to Ri [Rabbeinu Yitzchak] that when they seized it on their own he is also liable, for falling into the hand of the court is considered discernible damage; and since it fell into the hand of the court through negligence, he is liable and cannot say, "Here is yours before you," unlike leavened bread over which Passover has passed, which is indiscernible damage — therefore, there he can say, "Here is yours before you." And Rabbi Yaakov does not consider falling into the hand of the court and their issuing its verdict to be discernible damage, since even if it had not come into their hands they would have issued its verdict; thus it emerges that he does not lose through its coming into their hands, rather it is considered as though they issued its verdict in its absence, because even then it would have been forbidden [for benefit], and it is indiscernible damage — and therefore he can say to him, "Here is yours before you," just like with leavened bread over which Passover has passed. And [the phrase] "If you had returned it [to me, I would have smuggled it to the marsh]" is not giving a reason that he could have saved it thereby — for it does not depend on that, as Rashi explained — rather, [the Gemara] means to say: they would not have issued its verdict in its absence, and now you caused it to be seized in their hands, and they issue its verdict because it fell into their hands; and since it is lost because it fell into their hands, it is considered discernible damage, and you cannot say, "Here is yours before you." And so it is implied in [the chapter] HaNizakin (Gittin 53b) that with discernible damage one cannot say, "Here is yours before you," as [the Gemara] challenges from the Mishnah of "If one robbed a coin and it was disqualified, etc.": "And if you say indiscernible damage is called damage" — meaning, because it is considered as though it were discernible — "why does he say to him, 'Here is yours before you'? It is robbery, and he must pay good money!" — because this is not the money that he robbed, since it is considered as though the damage is discernible in it, for you have no greater change than this if it were discernible. And [regarding] an innocuous ox (shor tam) that causes damage while in the possession of a bailee, even before the verdict, if the bailee returns it to the owners he is not exempt thereby, since it caused damage through the bailee's negligence and fell into the possession of the injured party — to be immediately vested in him according to Rabbi Akiva to have a lien on it, or according to Rabbi Yishmael to collect from its body — and it is [therefore] discernible damage, since it is lost [to the owner] by having fallen into the possession of others, and he cannot say, "Here is yours before you," as he can say with an ox that killed even after the verdict according to Rabbi Yaakov, and according to the Rabbis before the verdict, and with leavened bread according to all opinions:

Tosafot on Bava Kamma 45a:8:1.hebrew: אלא שור בר טענה הוא - ואפילו דרשינן בעלמא "כמיתת בעלים כך מיתת השור", להך מילתא אין סברא לדירשו:
Tosafot on Bava Kamma 45a:8:1.english: But [as for] an ox, is it capable of presenting claims? - And even though we expound elsewhere, "like the death of the owner, so is the death of the ox," regarding this matter it is not logical to expound it [this way].

Tosafot on Bava Kamma 45a:9:1.hebrew: חוץ משומר חנם - הוא הדין דהוה מצי למימר: כולן פטורין בשמרו שמירה מעולה, חוץ משואל דחייב באונסים:
Tosafot on Bava Kamma 45a:9:1.english: With the exception of an unpaid bailee - Similarly, [the baraita] could have stated [that] all of them are exempt when they guarded [the ox] with superior guarding, except for a borrower, who is liable for unavoidable accidents.
